content: Efforts are being made to develop effective risk management strategies to address vaccine safety concerns. Technical assistance and subregional training sessions will be provided to immunization programs and medicine regulatory authorities. These sessions aim to integrate risk management approaches into existing vaccine post-marketing surveillance systems and, where necessary, strengthen vaccine safety monitoring systems. In addition to addressing vaccine safety, technical support will be offered to Member States to enhance healthcare providers' understanding of vaccine safety profiles and monitoring. This will include creating fact sheets, training materials, and practical advice to address parental concerns about vaccination. Despite significant progress in eliminating measles and rubella, outbreaks persist in the European Region. Between 2010 and 2012, over 100,000 measles cases were reported, peaking at 37,073 cases in 2011. Indigenous transmission of the measles virus continues in many countries, and rubella outbreaks remain in some endemic areas. Contributing factors include the accumulation of unvaccinated older children and young adults, low vaccination coverage in certain groups due to religious or philosophical beliefs, declining public acceptance of immunization, and health system reforms affecting immunization services. To improve outbreak response, Member States must develop action plans for detecting and responding to measles or rubella outbreaks. Regional guidelines on outbreak response are being developed to assist Member States in creating comprehensive national response plans. The European Immunization Week (EIW), established in 2005, has been an effective platform for promoting immunization awareness and increasing vaccination coverage, particularly among vulnerable groups. With participation from 53 Member States, EIW has become a visible pan-European health initiative. The Regional Office will continue to strengthen this platform annually. Healthcare workers play a critical role in providing parents with accurate information about vaccines and ensuring access to quality immunization services. The Regional Office will provide healthcare professionals with high-quality information on vaccines, vaccine-preventable diseases, and elimination goals through publications, reports, and online resources. Infographics and job aids will also be developed to support healthcare workers. Recognizing the importance of new communication technologies, the Regional Office is enhancing its online and social media presence to disseminate reliable vaccine information. A bloggers for health strategy will be implemented to engage online influencers in promoting accurate vaccine-related messages. Additionally, smartphone applications, such as vaccine reminder and tracker apps, are being developed to support immunization efforts. Vaccine safety communication guidelines and training are being developed to address vaccine safety scares and anti-vaccine claims. A training syllabus on vaccine safety communications will be piloted and implemented in subregional training sessions. The Regional Office will also provide ad-hoc safety communication support to Member States as needed. To achieve measles and rubella elimination, regional and global partnerships are essential. These partnerships will advocate for resources, provide technical assistance, and share best practices. The Regional Office plans to revitalize the MECACAR platform, which previously contributed to the interruption of wild poliovirus transmission, to strengthen measles and rubella elimination efforts through coordinated activities and cross-border collaboration. Verification of measles and rubella elimination progress is ongoing, with Member States responsible for collecting and analyzing epidemiological and laboratory data. Annual status reports are required to document progress. In summary, achieving measles and rubella elimination in the European Region requires a multifaceted approach, including strengthening immunization systems, improving outbreak response, enhancing communication strategies, leveraging partnerships, and maintaining robust verification processes.
